name: Atari 2600
description: Atari's Video Computer System, launched in 1977, popularised interchangeable game cartridges and brought arcade hits into living rooms. With almost no RAM and no frame buffer, programmers had to draw each scanline in step with the TV beam. It stayed on sale until 1992.
curiosities: It was sold as the Atari VCS until it was renamed the 2600 in 1982.
The 128 bytes of RAM live inside the 6532 RIOT chip, which also handles input and timers.
Early cartridges held only 2 KB or 4 KB; larger games used bank switching.
In 2014 excavators recovered E.T. cartridges from the 1983 landfill in Alamogordo, New Mexico.
Warren Robinett hid his name in a secret room in Adventure, one of the first known video game Easter eggs.
story: Atari built the Video Computer System to play many games on cartridges rather than one built in. Engineers Jay Miner and Joe Decuir designed its chip around a 6507; Nolan Bushnell sold Atari to Warner to pay for the launch, in September 1977.

It sold slowly at first, then Space Invaders under licence in 1980 made it the first console to be a hit thanks to a single game. Activision, founded by Atari programmers, became the first third-party publisher.
A flood of poor games, including Pac-Man and E.T., helped bring on the North American crash of 1983. Still, about 30 million units were sold, and its homebrew scene is busy today.
